decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and the blind coding classify this study as a replication. Wills et al. (2018) conducted a new multisite randomized controlled trial across 21 elementary schools and 157 classrooms in three states to conceptually replicate the first CW-FIT randomized controlled trial. corrected_value.title: Student and teacher outcomes of the class-wide function-related intervention team (CW-FIT) program

decisions.quote: The purpose of this study was to provide a close conceptual replication of the first CW-FIT RCT ( Wills et al., 2016 ) by using methods of the original study and following procedures as closely as possible ( Cook, 2014 ;  Coyne et al., 2016 ).
decisions.location: Purpose, paragraph 5 (see also Discussion and References)
decisions.reason: The shipped row named Kamps, Wills et al. (2015, DOI 10.1177/1098300714565244), which reported class-wide outcomes of the initial trial and was likely inferred from the uncited abstract summary. In the saved full-text manuscript (PMC10038329), the authors explicitly distinguish the class-wide RCT reports (Kamps, Wills et al., 2015; Wills et al., 2018) from the target-student efficacy report of the first CW-FIT RCT, Wills, Kamps, Fleming, & Hansen (2016, Exceptional Children 83:58-76, DOI 10.1177/0014402916658658), and repeatedly state in the Purpose, Method, and Discussion sections that the present study is a close conceptual replication of Wills et al. (2016) re-testing individual high-risk student and teacher outcomes (176 intervention and 148 comparison high-risk students vs. 181 and 132 in Wills et al., 2016). Blind target 0 is therefore right. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this key.

decisions.quote: Effects in this CW-FIT study provided a successful replication for student and teacher outcomes, indicating positive findings and significantly better performance for high-risk students in intervention classes than for those in the comparison classrooms ( Wills et al., 2016 ).
decisions.reason: Resolving the outcome dependency against the true replicated target Wills et al. (2016, DOI 10.1177/0014402916658658), the authors state an explicit overall verdict that the study provided a successful replication for student and teacher outcomes (Wills et al., 2016). Moreover, every primary tested finding compared with Wills et al. (2016)—increased target-student engagement (d = .94), reduced target-student disruptive behavior (d = .58), increased teacher praise (total d = 1.71; individual d = .249), and decreased teacher reprimands (total d = .21; individual d = .17), as well as improvements for Tier 2 participants and positive effects across sites and lower/upper grades—replicated in the predicted direction; under the codebook, smaller effect sizes for Tier 2 or site-level reprimand subanalyses do not alter the authors overall successful verdict. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this key.
